class.name: DirectionalLightShaft
class.brief_description: A [DirectionalLight] that also renders Unreal-style light shafts ("god rays").
class.description: DirectionalLightShaft behaves like a [DirectionalLight] but additionally drives a real screen-space light-shaft post-process in the GLES3 renderer, mirroring how Unreal Engine splits the effect: - [b]Light Shaft Bloom[/b] ([member bloom_enabled]): bright streaks radial-blurred outward from the light's on-screen position. - [b]Light Shaft Occlusion[/b] ([member occlusion_enabled]): the scene is darkened toward the light where geometry blocks it, using the depth buffer so real occluders (not just dark surfaces) cast the shafts. The pass downsamples the frame, builds the bloom and depth-occlusion masks, radial-blurs both toward the sun over several growing-radius iterations, temporally filters the result against the previous frame ([member temporal_blend]), then composites it back before glow and tone mapping. When the sun is off screen or behind the camera the effect costs nothing. This is a GLES3-only feature and requires the HDR/buffers rendering path (the same one glow and DOF use). On the GLES2 backend the node is an ordinary [DirectionalLight].

members.member: If [code]true[/code], bright streaks are scattered outward from the light.

Overall strength of the scattered streaks in the final composite. The additive contribution is capped relative to the local scene brightness so it can't detonate a downstream [Environment] glow HDR-bleed pass.
Brightness (in linear HDR) a pixel must exceed to contribute to the streaks. Keep it near or above [code]1.0[/code] so only the sun and its immediate glow scatter, not the whole sky.
Color the scattered streaks are multiplied by.
If [code]true[/code], the scene is darkened toward the light where geometry blocks it (depth-based).

How strongly the scene is dimmed toward the light where geometry blocks it. Localized to the light's on-screen region and floored, so it stays subtle. [code]0[/code] disables it. The bright streaks already carry their own gaps where blocked; this only adds the extra "dark shafts" cue.
Master switch. When [code]false[/code] the node is a plain [DirectionalLight].
Number of taps in the radial-blur gather. Higher is smoother/longer but costlier. See [enum ShaftQuality].
How far along the ray toward the light each tap reaches. Higher spreads the shafts further.
Per-tap falloff of the accumulated light along the ray.
Gain applied while accumulating the radial-blur samples (before the soft-knee). Raise for punchier streaks.

Fraction of the previous frame's result reprojected and kept each frame, to remove the last of the sampling grain. Off by default; any real camera motion drops it to zero automatically. Turn it up ([code]0.7[/code]–[code]0.9[/code]) for a mostly-static camera.

constants.constant: Suggested [member shaft_samples] for high quality (the default).
